sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Lesson 6.6 of Dataset Fundamentals: Detecting Data Issues—Paradoxes, Invariants, and Anomalies. Summary statistics frequently conceal catastrophic data pathologies behind reassuring means, variances, and aggregate correlations.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Today we build a rigorous causal and forensic defense suite. We will derive Simpson's reversal from Omitted Variable Bias and Pearl's backdoor adjustment, prove Berkson's collider odds ratio collapse, expose Anscombe and Datasaurus moment degeneracy, prove Benford's first-digit law from scale invariance, and contrast Tukey non-parametric fences against Chauvenet outlier masking.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Data issues split cleanly into two complementary audit domains. First, marginal versus conditional causal conflicts—whether aggregating across a hidden confounder causes Simpson's sign reversal, or filtering on a common effect triggers Berkson's selection bias.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Second, forensic distributional invariants—whether two completely distinct shapes share identical Anscombe moments, whether financial digits obey Benford's logarithmic mantissa law, and whether heavy-tailed outliers evade Gaussian Chauvenet filters through variance inflation.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's formalize Simpson's Paradox rigorously in both discrete probability and continuous regression. In a binary trial with treatment X, outcome Y, and stratum Z, treatment X can perform worse than control inside every individual stratum k, yet beat control marginally!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: By the Law of Total Probability, marginal risk equals a weighted sum over Z using treatment-specific weights P(Z equals k given X equals x). If severe patients disproportionately receive treatment X, confounded stratum weights overwhelm within-group reality.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In continuous OLS, omitting confounder Z shifts the slope by gamma times Cov(x, z) divided by Var(x). Whenever that Omitted Variable Bias opposes and exceeds the magnitude of beta true, the estimated slope flips sign—requiring Pearl's backdoor adjustment over P(Z equals z).

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Whereas Simpson's Paradox stems from omitting a common cause Z, Berkson's Paradox strikes when analysts condition on a common effect C—known in causal graphs as a collider: X points to C and Y points to C.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Suppose two independent diseases X and Y occur with population probabilities p X and p Y, so their true Odds Ratio is 1.0. Now suppose a patient enters a hospital dataset C equals 1 if and only if they have X or Y or both.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Among admitted patients with C equals 1, knowing an individual has disease Y drops their probability of X to p X—while knowing they lack Y forces X to be 1.0 with certainty to explain admission! Thus conditional Odds Ratio collapses strictly below 1, explaining why diagnostic AI trained purely on inpatient records falsely learns negative diabetes-hypertension risk.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Even when causality is completely clean, aggregate descriptive moments can be completely blind to geometry. In 1973, Francis Anscombe constructed four distinct bivariate datasets sharing identical mean X of 9.0, variance 11.0, mean Y of 7.50, variance 4.125, Pearson r of 0.816, and OLS line y equals 3.00 plus 0.50x.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Yet plotting them exposes four incompatible realities: a Gaussian linear cloud, a noiseless concave parabola, a straight line distorted by one vertical outlier, and a vertical column warped by a single extreme-leverage point. Matejka and Fitzmaurice pushed this further in 2017 with the Datasaurus Dozen via simulated annealing—proving stars, rings, and dinosaurs can match summary metrics to two decimals.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 1: the Simpson's Paradox and Causal Omitted Variable Bias Studio. Notice our three stratified patient cohorts plotted in teal, gold, and emerald—every subgroup slopes negatively downward with true slope beta true equals minus 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: When confounder shift magnitude gamma sits at 25.0, pooling all cohorts without conditioning flips the red aggregate regression line positive! Drag the sliders and click the Simpson OVB Lab pill below to drive gamma toward zero and observe Omitted Variable Bias vanish.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's test your causal conditioning intuition on Checkpoint 1. Review two hospital findings below: first, Drug X loses to placebo inside both Mild and Severe patient strata yet wins in marginal totals; second, inpatient records show negative correlation between diabetes and hypertension.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Turning now to forensic invariants: Frank Benford noticed in 1938 that across natural datasets spanning orders of magnitude—financial invoices, census populations, river basin areas—leading digits are never uniform.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Digit 1 appears 30.10 percent of the time, while digit 9 appears only 4.58 percent. Why? Universal physical or monetary laws must be scale-invariant—converting dollars to euros or kilometers to miles cannot alter the first-digit distribution!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Solving f(cx) times c equals f(x) gives f(x) proportional to 1 over x. Taking base-10 logarithm maps scale multiplication into modular translation, forcing mantissa log base 10 of X mod 1 to be Uniform on [0, 1)—whose integral from log 10(d) to log 10(d+1) yields log base 10 of (1 + 1/d).

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To operationalize Benford's Law across ingested ledgers or telemetry, we compute Pearson's Chi-Square statistic across the nine leading digits with 8 degrees of freedom: sum of (O d minus E d) squared divided by E d, where E d equals n times log 10(1 + 1/d).

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: A rejection at p less than 0.05 flags manual invention, reimbursement thresholding, or sensor clipping. Crucially, however, engineers must verify domain prerequisites first: Benford requires positive scale-free quantities spanning multiple orders of magnitude—never narrowly bounded metrics like human body temperature around 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Section 5 contrasts two classical univariate outlier criteria. Chauvenet's Criterion assumes a Gaussian distribution N(mu, sigma squared) and rejects x i whenever n times complementary error function erfc(|x i minus x bar| over root 2 times s) drops below 0.5.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: On heavy-tailed streams like network latency or lognormal bursts, Chauvenet commits two fatal errors: first, over-rejecting valid Pareto tails; second, outlier masking—because sample standard deviation s has zero breakdown point, one extreme spike inflates denominator root 2 s so secondary outliers vanish!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Tukey's non-parametric fences—Inner 1.5 IQR and Outer 3.0 IQR—rely on quartiles Q1 and Q3 whose 25 percent breakdown point resists heavy tails and eliminates variance-inflation masking cleanly.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's examine two classic real-world studies from the textbook. First, the 1973 UC Berkeley graduate admissions study by Bickel, Hammel, and O'Connell: aggregate numbers showed 44.3 percent acceptance for men versus 34.6 percent for women—a 9.7 percentage-point gap with p below 10 to the negative 6.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Yet conditioning across Departments A through F revealed zero anti-female bias—in four of six departments women were admitted at higher rates, including 82 versus 62 percent in Department A! Department competitiveness was the hidden confounder driving Simpson's Paradox.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Second, an enterprise audit of 42,000 employee travel claims cleared manual controls because every item fell under the 100-dollar per-diem cap. Yet Benford's Law exposed digit 9 spiking to 31.8 percent versus 4.6 percent expected—chi-square 3,412.8—catching mass forging around 95 to 99.50 dollars!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 2: our Benford Forensic Auditor Workbench. In default Authentic Lognormal Ledger mode, observed digit bars trace the theoretical Benford logarithmic curve closely, passing Pearson chi-square at 8 degrees of freedom with p above 0.05.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Now switch Audited Ledger Profile to Sub-Cap Threshold Fraud at 95 to 99.50 dollars or Fabricated Uniform Numbers, and watch digit 9 or flat uniform columns smash chi-square above hundreds and trigger an immediate red fraud alert!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 2. First, consider converting audited corporate travel claims from US dollars into euros before checking whether digit 9 hits 31.8 percent; second, compare Chauvenet's Criterion against Tukey's outer fence on a heavy-tailed latency stream with one plus 50 sigma corruption.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Section 6 delivers a Pydantic V2 production module, data_pathology_suite.py, enforcing typed telemetry contracts across ingestion jobs. SimpsonAuditReport logs marginal correlation, OLS slope, per-stratum correlations, Omitted Variable Bias, and triggers simpsons_paradox_detected whenever every subgroup opposes the marginal sign.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Meanwhile BenfordAuditReport requires n at least 50 strictly positive values, maps leading base-10 digits into observed counts versus expected n times log 10(1 + 1/d), evaluates SciPy chisquare over 8 degrees of freedom, and separates authentic lognormal streams from uniform fabricated runs.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Before concluding, let's unify all five failure modes into one engineering matrix. Omitted confounders cause Simpson sign reversals and demand backdoor stratification; collider conditioning creates Berkson selection bias and forbids filtering on common consequences.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Moment degeneracy across Anscombe and Datasaurus requires direct residual and scatter visualization; fabricated figures trigger Benford's chi-square digit test over 8 degrees of freedom; and heavy-tailed outlier masking is eliminated by Tukey's 25-percent-breakdown fences.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's seal Lesson 6.6 with four Cardinal Production Rules for detecting data issues before training or policy deployment. First, stratify and adjust via Pearl's backdoor formula so omitted confounders never flip signs. Second, audit selection filters for Berkson colliders before learning comorbidities.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Third, never rely on summary scalar moments alone—pair metrics with direct geometry and residual checks to catch Anscombe degeneracy. Fourth, deploy scale-free Benford chi-square digit audits alongside 25-percent-breakdown Tukey quartile fences. Next up in Lesson 6.7: automating your complete EDA Workflow and Profiling Pipeline!
